statements.justification: MTTP microarray and proteomics values match exactly, but asserting HNF1A's own transcript is 'unchanged' ('rather than a loss of the HNF1A transcript itself') directly contradicts Wang 2019 Figure 2C qPCR showing severe HNF1A mRNA loss in DBD Mut (p < 0.0001) and reduction in SUMO Mut (p < 0.05).

All APOB fold changes, omic layers, axis specificity (DBD-only collapse), and citation [1] in statement S2 are accurate (with a minor caveat only in the expanded prose repeating the microarray-based HNF1A unchanged note).

CDH1 protein drops strongly in both axes and mRNA drops in SUMOmut, but DBDmut_vs_WT mRNA (-1.38-fold, log2 -0.46, p = 0.063) is neither statistically significant nor a DEG, refuting 'down in both axes at both mRNA and protein level' ('markedly down in both mutants at both levels').

ITGB5 mRNA is significantly downregulated in both mutants (p = 2.06e-5 and 1.38e-5; < 2-fold cutoff), refuting 'falls at the protein level only', and ITGB5 protein in SUMOmut (-2.02) is not marked significant in Table S3 (''), refuting prose's concordant both-axes claim.

Fully accurate data, contrasts, and citations [5],[6], and uncovers a novel 12.2-fold post-transcriptional collapse of the clathrin cargo adaptor DAB2 in DBDmut that was completely missed in Wang 2019 despite directly linking to the paper's highlighted LDLR, LRP2, and fibrinogen (FGA) defects.

Statement S6 itself is true across proteomics, ER-cycle biology, and citation [7], and highlights a genuine ER quality-control module omitted from Wang 2019; kept at 'Makes sense' rather than 'Especially good' because the backing prose over-interprets the <2-fold DEG filter by calling GANAB and CALR 'protein level only' despite significant p < 0.01 mRNA decreases.

Biologically true and faithfully grounded in [8] and [11], but statement S7 itself is purely generic literature background that mentions nothing about Wang 2019's experiment, HNF4A perturbations, contrasts, or data (and cites iPSC-derived hepatocytes from [8] rather than H9 hESCs).

Major multi-error anchor failure: misattributes Wang 2019's HNF4A DBD deletion to loss of HNF1A transactivation (X), asserts HNF1A abundance is unchanged/flat contrary to Figure 2C qPCR p < 0.0001 collapse (D), and misuses HNF1A POU-mutant [10] and Hnf1a-/- KO [9] papers (C).

overall.comment: Two statements make sense (S2 APOB, S6 ER quality-control module), one is especially good (S5 uncovers a 12.2-fold post-transcriptional DAB2 protein loss in DBDmut linking to LDLR/LRP2/FGA), and five do not make sense: S1 and S8 assert HNF1A mRNA is unchanged from microarray noise despite Fig. 2C qPCR collapse and S8 misattributes the HNF4A DBD deletion to HNF1A with inverted citations; S3 and S4 misstate mRNA/protein significance for CDH1 and ITGB5; and S7 is generic background unrelated to this experiment.
